back: In a closed system, the forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates, so the concentrations of all species stay constant.
If the conditions of a system in dynamic equilibrium are changed, the position of equilibrium moves to oppose the change.
Higher pressure moves the position to the side with fewer moles of gas; no effect if the numbers of moles of gas are equal.
Higher temperature moves the position in the endothermic direction; lower temperature in the exothermic direction.
Speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally: equilibrium reached sooner, no change in position, yield or K.

front: What changes the value of K?
back: Only temperature. Concentration and pressure change the position but not K.
CrO₄²⁻ is yellow, Cr₂O₇²⁻ is orange; adding acid gives orange, adding alkali gives yellow.
Products must stay in contact with the reactants so the reverse reaction can occur; an open system lets gases escape.
CO₂(g) ⇌ CO₂(aq): opening the bottle lowers the pressure, so CO₂ comes out of solution.
